Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the rear-end collision you
were involved in while driving in Pasadena, Texas. Do you understand that this call is being recorded?
A: Yes, I understand.
Q: Please state your full name and the best number to reach you.
A: I'd rather keep my personal details off the recording for now, but I can give you a callback number through the
claim file.
Q: That works. Can you walk me through what happened leading up to the collision?
A: I was stopped at a red light on a main road heading toward the freeway. It was a nomral afternoon, traffic was
moderate. The light was red and I had come to a complete stop behind a silver sedan.
Q: How long were you stopped before the impact?
A: Probably ten or fifteen seconds. Long enough that I had fully stopped and was waiting for the light.
Q: What happened next?
A: I felt a hard jolt from behind. My car was pushed forward into the sedan in front of me. My head snapped back and
then forward, and my right hand hit the steering wheel.
Q: Did you notice anything about the vehicle bheind you before the impact?
A: I checked my mirror a moment before stopping and saw a pickup truck approaching fast. I didn't have time to react
after that.
Q: Did you seek medical attention?
A: Yes, I was taken to the emergency room that evening. They X-rayed my right wrist and told me it was fractured.
I've been wearing a splint and I'm scheduled for follow-up with an orthopedic specialist.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add about the collision or your injuries?
A: Only that my wrist has limited my ability to work and drive comfortably. I'm willing to provide the medical records.
Q: Thank you. We'll follow up with you about those records. This concludes the statement.
A: Thank you.
</page>

"policy_numbers" = only values labeled as a policy number. A claim number is not a policy number.
"street" and "city" = the person's own home address, only if the page gives it. Never use the
address of a clinic, shop, firm or court for a person.
"loss_dates" = only a date that the page clearly gives as the date of the accident, crash, loss or
injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.
"words_before" = the words written on the page directly before that date, copied exactly, that say
it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
